Usage
  loupe capture [<pr-url> | --changed | --files <path>... | --no-files --title <title>] [flags]

Capture a GitHub pull request into a new review round.

Resolves the pull request through the GitHub API, verifies that the clone's origin is the
pull request's repository, fetches base and head into private refs under refs/loupe/,
stores the diff and its SHA-256, and creates an empty draft. The working files, index,
current branch and every other ref of the clone are left untouched.

It also finds the round loupe show --previous will list. An earlier local round with a
receipt from the same publisher wins. Without one, capture reads the publisher's newest
loupe review on the pull request back from GitHub, the viewer's own, or with an App token
a [bot]'s whose source name matches --source, and stores its findings in the run, so loupe
show --previous answers offline. A review that cannot be read back, or a listing that fails,
is stored as a reason instead, marked unreadable. That never refuses the capture.

It also reads everyone else's feedback on the pull request for loupe show --comments:
submitted reviews, inline review threads and top-level comments, every page of each. It
leaves out loupe's own reviews for this source: a loupe review whose source name, version
aside, matches --source and whose author is the viewer, or with an App token a [bot]. A
listing that fails is stored as a reason, never as empty lists.

A closed pull request, merged or not, is refused with pr unless --allow-closed is given.
With it, capture runs as for an open one. target.prState records the state GitHub
reported, open or closed, so a reader can tell a closed pull request's run apart.

The clone is --repo, or the working directory.

At most once a day, a capture also looks up loupe's latest release. If it is newer than this
build, capture warns on stderr and lists update-available in the result's warnings. A lookup
that fails never refuses the capture. LOUPE_NO_UPDATE_CHECK=1 turns this off.

Result (--json)
  {"loupe": 1, "ok": true, "command": "capture", "run": "owner/repo#123@1",
   "dir": "/path/to/run", "version": 0,
   "target": {"schema": 3, "owner": "owner", "repo": "repo", "number": 123,
              "url": "https://github.com/owner/repo/pull/123", "title": "...", "author": "...",
              "viewer": "...", "baseSha": "...", "headSha": "...", "round": 1,
              "capturedAt": "2026-09-13T12:00:00Z", "clonePath": "/path/to/clone",
              "baseRef": "refs/loupe/owner/repo/123/1/base", "headRef": "refs/loupe/owner/repo/123/1/head",
              "mergeBaseSha": "...", "diffSha256": "...", "source": "my-reviewer@1.0.0",
              "model": "anthropic/claude-sonnet-5", "prState": "open"},
   "refs": {"base": "refs/loupe/owner/repo/123/1/base", "head": "refs/loupe/owner/repo/123/1/head"},
   "cleanup": ["git -C /path/to/clone update-ref -d refs/loupe/owner/repo/123/1/base",
               "git -C /path/to/clone update-ref -d refs/loupe/owner/repo/123/1/head"],
   "next": ["loupe add --run owner/repo#123@1 --from <file> --json",
            "loupe summary --run owner/repo#123@1 --from <file> --expect-findings <n> --json",
            "then the human runs: loupe review owner/repo#123@1"],
   "previous": {"from": "github", "round": 1, "head": "...",
                "reviewUrl": "https://github.com/owner/repo/pull/123#pullrequestreview-123", "findingCount": 2},
   "comments": {"read": true, "reviews": 2, "threads": 1, "comments": 3}}
  target.previousRound is present from round 2 on; target.source only when --source was given, and target.model only
  when --model was. previous.from is receipt (with round), github (with round, reviewUrl and findingCount) or none
  (with reason, and unreadable: true when a loupe review exists but cannot be read back, or the reviews could not be
  listed). previous.head, the commit the previous round reviewed, is present with receipt or github unless it could
  not be read back. Run loupe show --previous when it is receipt or github. comments is {read: true} with the three
  counts, or {read: false, reason}. Run loupe show --comments when read is true. warnings, an array of
  warning codes, appears only when nonempty.

Local work (apply mode) is captured instead into a local run, local#<n>, whose decisions go back
to the agent rather than to GitHub. It makes no network call, and warns of a newer release only
from what an earlier pull request capture found:
  --changed [--base <ref>]    the worktree's staged, unstaged and untracked changes against HEAD,
                              or against the merge base with --base, read through a temporary
                              index so the user's index, refs and files stay untouched
  --files <path>...           each file whole; repeat --files for more
  --no-files --title <title>  no file, for findings that are all general
Each takes --title and --applier, the name of who applies the decisions. Binary, empty, deleted,
submodule and files over 1 MiB are listed under local.skipped instead of captured.

Result for a local run (--json):
  {"loupe": 1, "ok": true, "command": "capture", "run": "owner/repo:local#7",
   "dir": "/path/to/run", "version": 0,
   "target": {"schema": 3, "kind": "local", "title": "...", "applier": "Claude",
              "capturedAt": "...", "diffSha256": "...",
              "local": {"n": 7, "prefix": "owner/repo", "repository": "owner/repo",
                        "capture": "changed", "root": "/path/to/worktree", "branch": "feat/x",
                        "baseRef": "main", "mergeBase": "...",
                        "files": [{"path": "docs/plan.md", "abs": "/path/to/worktree/docs/plan.md"},
                                  {"path": "notes.txt", "abs": "...", "new": true}],
                        "skipped": [{"path": "logo.png", "reason": "binary"}]}},
   "headings": {"docs/plan.md": [{"heading": "Goals", "level": 2, "line": 3}]},
   "next": ["loupe add --run owner/repo:local#7 --from <file> --json",
            "loupe handoff --run owner/repo:local#7 --json"]}
  Anchor findings to local.files[].path. headings lists each captured Markdown file's headings.

Flags
      --allow-closed[=true|false]   accept a closed or merged pull request; without it capture refuses one with pr
      --applier string              who will apply a local run's decisions, as the human knows them, at most 64 characters
      --base string                 with --changed, diff against the merge base of HEAD and this ref instead of HEAD
      --changed[=true|false]        capture the changed files of the current Git worktree: staged, unstaged and untracked, against HEAD or --base
      --files stringArray           capture this file whole; repeat for more files
  -h, --help[=true|false]           help for capture
      --model string                the model that produces the findings, as you name it, matching ^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9._/:-]*$, at most 64 characters, no --; recorded in the published review's footer and loupe-meta, never required
      --no-files[=true|false]       capture no file, for findings that are all general; needs --title
      --repo string                 path to a clone of the pull request's repository (default: the working directory)
      --source string               the tool filing the findings, as name[@version]; shown in the published review's footer
      --title string                a local run's title, one line of at most 120 characters
      --json[=true|false]   print exactly one JSON result object on stdout

Examples
  loupe capture https://github.com/owner/repo/pull/123 --json
  loupe capture https://github.com/owner/repo/pull/123 --repo ~/src/repo
  loupe capture https://github.com/owner/repo/pull/123 --allow-closed --json
  loupe capture --changed --base main --json
  loupe capture --files docs/plan.md --applier Claude --json
